key_insight: Reduced-order polynomial models paired with quantum transport preserve nonlinear flow dynamics while making per-step rotation counts polylogarithmic in grid resolution at fixed model dimension and drift degree.
engineering_relevance: Jointly choosing reduced-model accuracy and polynomial degree offers a route to balancing flow-simulation fidelity against early fault-tolerant quantum hardware costs.
method: Fit polynomial reduced-order dynamics using sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics.
Encode probability-density evolution with Walsh-synthesized Koopman–von Neumann transport.
Estimate end-to-end costs using surface-code resource models.
evidence_signal: For a saturating cylinder wake, the study estimates 1.62 hours on about 560,000 physical qubits for 1% relative RMS field error against the radial model, and demonstrates nonlinear radial transport on IBM hardware with reference-circuit noise mitigation.
watch_item: The fault-tolerant runtimes are estimates, not hardware demonstrations; three-coordinate wake estimates range from hours to weeks, and the quoted 1% error is relative to the radial model.
paper_title: Nonlinearity-preserving quantum simulation of flows in the early fault-tolerant regime
